'''Riccardo Rattazzi''' (born 1964) is an Italian theoretical physicist and a professor at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]]. His main research interests are in [[physics beyond the Standard Model]] and in [[Physical cosmology|cosmology]].

== Career ==
Rattazzi studied physics at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]] and at the [[University of Pisa]], where he received the [[Laurea|Laurea cum laude]] in 1987. He carried out graduate research at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]] under the guidance of [[Riccardo Barbieri]]. He held postdoctoral positions at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1992-1993), at the [[Rutgers University]] (1993-1996), and at [[CERN]] (1996-1998). In 1998, he became a permanent researcher at the [[INFN|Instituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]] in Pisa. From 2001 to 2006, he was a junior staff member of the theoretical physics department at CERN. Since 2006 he holds a professorship of physics at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://lptp.epfl.ch/Rattazzi|title = Riccardo Rattazzi's webpage at the EPFL|date = |website = |publisher = |last = |first = }}</ref> He's also a Distinguished Visiting Research Chair at the Perimeter Institute of Theoretical Physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Riccardo Rattazzi at the Perimeter Institute of Theoretical Physics |url=https://perimeterinstitute.ca/people/riccardo-rattazzi |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>

On 7 October 2024, a conference<ref>{{Cite web |title=QFT Paniscia: Goldstones, bootstrap, fluids and flavours, alla novarese |url=https://indico.cern.ch/event/1451031/overview}}</ref> in honour of Rattazzi's 60th birthday took place at the EPFL.

== Main scientific discoveries ==
In 1998, together with [[Gian Francesco Giudice|Gian Giudice]], [[Markus Luty]] and Hitoshi Murayama, Rattazzi discovered the [[anomaly mediated supersymmetry breaking]], a subtle quantum mechanical mechanism which contributes to the [[gaugino]] masses in [[supergravity]].<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1088/1126-6708/1998/12/027| volume = 1998| issue = 12| page = 027| last1 = Giudice| first1 = Gian F.| last2 = Luty| first2 = Markus A.| last3 = Murayama| first3 = Hitoshi| last4 = Rattazzi| first4 = Riccardo| title = Gaugino mass without singlets| journal = JHEP| date = 1998| arxiv = hep-ph/9810442| bibcode = 1998JHEP...12..027G| s2cid = 12517291}}</ref>

In 1999, together with [[Gian Francesco Giudice|Giudice]] and [[James Wells (physicist)|James Wells]], Rattazzi carried out the first detailed study of the collider signatures of the [[large extra dimension]] scenarios of [[TeV]]-scale gravity.<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1016/S0550-3213(99)00044-9| volume = B544| issue = 1–2| pages = 3–38| last1 = Giudice| first1 = Gian F.| last2 = Rattazzi| first2 = Riccardo| last3 = Wells| first3 = James D.| title = Quantum gravity and extra dimensions at high-energy colliders| journal = Nucl. Phys.| date = 1999| arxiv = hep-ph/9811291| bibcode = 1999NuPhB.544....3G| s2cid = 14407490}}</ref>

In 2001, together with [[Alberto Zaffaroni]], Rattazzi gave the holographic description of the [[Randall-Sundrum]] solution of the hierarchy problem, as well as interpreted the [[Goldberger-Wise mechanism]] in terms of [[dimensional transmutation]].<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1088/1126-6708/2001/04/021| volume = 2001| issue = 4| page = 021| last1 = Rattazzi| first1 = R.| last2 = Zaffaroni| first2 = A.| title = Comments on the holographic picture of the Randall-Sundrum model| journal = JHEP| date = 2001| arxiv = hep-th/0012248| bibcode = 2001JHEP...04..021R| s2cid = 5549726}}</ref>

In 2004, together with [[Riccardo Barbieri|Barbieri]], [[Alex Pomarol]] and [[Alessandro Strumia]], Rattazzi laid out a conceptually clear and practically useful framework for the analysis of the combined electroweak precision data of the low- and high-energy phases of the [[Large Electron–Positron Collider|LEP]] experiments.<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2004.10.014| volume = B703| issue = 1–2| pages = 127–146| last1 = Barbieri| first1 = Riccardo| last2 = Pomarol| first2 = Alex| last3 = Rattazzi| first3 = Riccardo| last4 = Strumia| first4 = Alessandro| title = Electroweak symmetry breaking after LEP-1 and LEP-2| journal = Nucl. Phys.| date = 2004| arxiv = hep-ph/0405040| bibcode = 2004NuPhB.703..127B| s2cid = 14746575}}</ref>

In 2006, together with [[Allan Adams]], [[Nima Arkani-Hamed]], [[Sergei Dubovsky]] and [[Alberto Nicolis]], Rattazzi discovered surprising inconsistencies which may be present in the effective [[Lagrangian (field theory)|Lagrangian]]s in [[quantum field theory]]. These inconsistencies cannot be observed in empty space and at low energies, but they become apparent as violations of [[Causality problem|causality]] when many field [[quantum|quanta]] are present, or when one attempts to extend the theory to arbitrarily high energies.<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1088/1126-6708/2006/10/014| volume = 2006| issue = 10| page = 014| last1 = Adams| first1 = Allan| last2 = Arkani-Hamed| first2 = Nima| last3 = Dubovsky| first3 = Sergei| last4 = Nicolis| first4 = Alberto| last5 = Rattazzi| first5 = Riccardo| title = Causality, analyticity and an IR obstruction to UV completion| journal = JHEP| date = 2006| arxiv = hep-th/0602178| bibcode = 2006JHEP...10..014A| s2cid = 2956810}}</ref>

In 2007, together with [[Gian Francesco Giudice|Giudice]], [[Christoph Grojean]] and [[Alex Pomarol|Pomarol]], Rattazzi constructed a low-energy effective [[Lagrangian (field theory)|Lagrangian]] which encapsulated general properties of composite [[Higgs boson]] models in a way practically useful for the upcoming [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] experiments.<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1088/1126-6708/2007/06/045| volume = 2007| issue = 6| page = 045| last1 = Giudice| first1 = G. F.| last2 = Grojean| first2 = C.| last3 = Pomarol| first3 = A.| last4 = Rattazzi| first4 = R.| title = The Strongly-Interacting Light Higgs| journal = JHEP| date = 2007| arxiv = hep-ph/0703164| bibcode = 2007JHEP...06..045G| s2cid = 15292325}}</ref>

In 2008, together with [[Vyacheslav Rychkov|Slava Rychkov]], [[Erik Tonni]] and [[Alessandro Vichi]], Riccardo Rattazzi found the first practical implementation of the [[conformal bootstrap]] method in four-dimensional [[conformal field theories]]. While this work was motivated by physics beyond the standard model, it also proved influential in other areas of theoretical physics such as [[string theory]] and [[statistical physics]].<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1088/1126-6708/2008/12/031| volume = 2008| issue = 12| page = 031| last1 = Rattazzi| first1 = Riccardo| last2 = Rychkov| first2 = Vyacheslav S.| last3 = Tonni| first3 = Erik| last4 = Vichi| first4 = Alessandro| title = Bounding scalar operator dimensions in 4D CFT| journal = JHEP| date = 2008| arxiv = 0807.0004| bibcode = 2008JHEP...12..031R| s2cid = 8954304}}</ref>

In 2009, together with [[Alberto Nicolis|Nicolis]] and [[Enrico Trincherini]], Rattazzi discovered the [[galileon]]s, a new class of derivatively coupled [[scalar field theory|scalar field theories]] invariant under the [[Galilean transformation]]s. These theories have since proved useful in the theoretical study of early-universe cosmology and of [[dark energy]].<ref>{{Cite journal| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevD.79.064036| volume = D79| issue = 6| article-number = 064036| last1 = Nicolis| first1 = Alberto| last2 = Rattazzi| first2 = Riccardo| last3 = Trincherini| first3 = Enrico| title = The Galileon as a local modification of gravity| journal = Phys. Rev.| date = 2009| arxiv = 0811.2197| bibcode = 2009PhRvD..79f4036N| s2cid = 18168398}}</ref>
